references.text: The Lord predicts that He will harden Pharaoh's heart, so that he will not let the people go.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh hardened his own heart and did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh hardened his heart again this time and would not let the people go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had told Moses.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not let the children of Israel go, just as the Lord had said through Moses.
The Lord says that He has hardened Pharaoh's heart and the hearts of his servants.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel leave his land.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he pursued the children of Israel.
Paul quotes God's words to Pharaoh and explains that God hardens whom He wills, as an example of God's sovereignty.
A complementary perspective showing how God's hardening and Pharaoh's own hardening interact in the same conflict.
A prophetic precursor establishing that Pharaoh's hardness was an existing condition before God's active intervention.
A complementary perspective showing Pharaoh's active choice to harden himself when he was given a reprieve.
